archive.citation: N. Rivano, N. Marzari, T. Sohier, npj Comput. Mater. 9, 194 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41524-023-01140-2
archive.README.txt:
CONTENTS
================================

This repository contains the primary inputs and outputs of ab-initio calculations performed using the standard Quantum ESPRESSO code with 3D periodic boundary conditions, as well as its modified version designed for 1D systems. The modifications include a 1D Coulomb cutoff and a 1D dipole-dipole correction integrated into the Fourier phonon interpolation scheme.

================================
DATA
================================
Folder containing the main data. Main folders are:

1) BN_atomic_chain.
2) BN_nanotubes: 44, 55, 66 (referring to armchair tubes of different radius).
3) GaAs_nanowire.
4) GaAs_bulk: ZB_phase, WZ_phase.

Each of these directories contains the essential files required to replicate Figures 1, 2, and 3 from the main paper using (a) the standard QE code (3D_code) and (b) the modified version (1D code). These files encompass: inputs and outputs of the primary self-consistent field (SCF) calculation with pw.x, inputs and outputs of the phonon calculation with ph.x, and the generated files containing the dynamical matrix at each q-point. Additionally, inputs and outputs of q2r.x and matdyn.x are provided when used for phonon interpolation, along with the matdyn.modes files. The pseudopotentials employed for all materials are also included.

================================
CODES
================================

Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Density Functional Perturbation Theory (DFPT) calculations with 3D periodic-boundary conditions (PBCs) were conducted using the open-source software QE [1]. The modification of the standard code to accommodate 1D open-boundary conditions will be accessible at https://github.com/normarivano, pending its integration into the official branch. Detailed information about this modification can be found in an upcoming publication [2]. The release of this open-source code is planned following the acceptance of the manuscript.

[1] Giannozzi, P. et al. Quantum espresso: a modular and open-source software project for quantum simulations of materials. J. Condens. Matter Phys. 21, 395502 (2009).
[2] Rivano, N., Marzari, N. & Sohier, T. Density-functional perturbation theory for one-dimensional systems: implementation and relevance for phonons and electron-phonon interactions -- in preparation (2023).

**This file is automatically generated. It contains the descriptions of each uploaded file as provided by the user.**
* **materialscloud_data_Rivano.zip**: This repository contains input files, output files and scripts for reproducing the results of the article of the same name.

systems.BN_atomic_chain: BN atomic chain (polyyne-like B-N chain), 2 atoms per cell
systems.BN_nanotubes/44: armchair BN nanotube (4,4), 16 atoms per cell
systems.BN_nanotubes/55: armchair BN nanotube (5,5), 20 atoms per cell [hidden-target system]
systems.BN_nanotubes/66: armchair BN nanotube (6,6), 24 atoms per cell [hidden-target system]
systems.GaAs_nanowire: H-passivated wurtzite GaAs nanowire, 24 atoms per cell (the archived titles say 84)

  prefix='bn_chain',

conventions.dyn files: Quantum ESPRESSO ph.x fildyn format, as archived: q in cartesian units of 2pi/alat with alat = celldm(1) (the lateral cell size for ibrav 6, given in the header for ibrav 0); force-constant matrices in Ry/bohr^2 per atom pair (not mass-scaled); masses in Rydberg units (amu x 911.444); Gamma files of the 1D systems also carry the dielectric tensor of the simulation cell and the Born effective charges (E-U: [field][displacement]).
conventions.boundary conditions: '1D' = the authors' modified Quantum ESPRESSO with a 1D Coulomb cutoff (folders 1D_code); '3D' = standard 3D-periodic Quantum ESPRESSO on the same supercell (folders 3D_code).
conventions.interpolated: archived q2r/matdyn interpolations along Gamma-Z (matdyn.in shows the settings).

dfpt.returns: the archived dynamical-matrix file as text

interpolated.returns: frequencies along Gamma-Z and the axial share of each mode, parsed from the archived matdyn.modes

archived_file.returns: an archived pw.x/ph.x/q2r.x/matdyn.x output as text (first 400000 characters)

withheld: BN(5,5) and BN(6,6), 1D boundary conditions: the archived explicit small-q runs below 0.15 |Gamma-Z| (longwave folders and their copies)
